blind_comparisons.question: Which timeline shows a player whose invulnerability is AIMED at the enemy weapon rather than sprayed near it — a high X:i ratio and few bare H columns?
blind_comparisons.blind_rationale: Every invulnerable column in A touches an enemy-hitbox column — there is no free-standing `i` anywhere in the strip — and the `iXi` groupings read as an i-frame window that opened before the weapon arrived and closed after it left. B contains three `i` columns immediately followed by a bare `H`, which is invulnerability that arrived a beat early and had expired when the blade landed, and B's unanswered swings are scattered singletons with no structure while A's come in pairs, which is what eating the second and third hits of a string looks like.

rerun.method: CRITIC-DOCTRINE §2.5 step 2 — re-measure at frame resolution rather than 20-frame columns, and add a second discriminator the item names: the distance from each invulnerable frame to the nearest enemy hitbox-active frame.
rerun.result: Coverage of enemy hitbox-active frames by player invulnerability is 0.516-0.622 across the five fights against round 2's 0.135-0.275 — a real improvement, and the reason the coarse pack favoured ours. But the 90th-percentile distance from an invulnerable frame to the nearest enemy hitbox frame is 58-96 f@60 against round 2's 62-104, with 803-1014 invulnerable frames per fight for only 360-443 enemy active frames. The player is invulnerable for more than twice as long as anything is trying to hit it.

blind_comparisons.not_possible_reason: Degenerate pair, re-filed from rounds 1 and 2: both sides of a roll-frame-census pack coincide exactly when the work is correct, so the pack cannot discriminate. The sharper discriminator — the roll's per-frame root-delta curve — is filed again under corpus_extended.

Lock-on is judged on camera behaviour and this critic declared the axis not-visual; no non-visual pair exists.
The item's pack is two 60 s dist_m + state series from a real enemy AI. There is no enemy AI in this build (W1-12); a pack would compare a script against a behaviour model.

biggest_gap.what: The round-2 hole in the weapon volume is untouched; it has been covered by a second volume that pays the weapon's damage. Ablation, measured on a copy of the loaded data with no file edited: delete `hitgeometry.json §body_hazard` and the champion's minimum reaching distance against a stationary player returns to chop 1.2 m, thrust 1.6 m, combo_a 1.1 m, combo_b 1.2 m — round 2's numbers to the decimal. With the block present, every hit inside those radii carries `via: "body"`, and a body hit deals the attack's full weapon damage: chop 96 at 0.05 m via body is the same 96 as at 3.65 m via weapon, thrust 75, combo_a 63. It is the same on the player's side — the dagger's blade cannot cut inside 0.75 m and the straight sword's inside 0.80 m, so 14 of the dagger's 19 connecting distances and 15 of the straight sword's 36 are torso-checks. Two of the seven player classes fail S26's contiguity clause outright, and the gaps sit exactly at the seam between the two volumes: the spear's body corridor stops at 1.15 m and its blade starts at 1.30 m, leaving 1.20-1.25 m dead; the halberd's stops at 1.10 m and starts at 1.35 m, leaving 1.15-1.30 m dead. Reproduced identically in headless Chromium and in the node arena. And it is what the fight is made of: in the shipping game, 5 to 7 of the 8 blows that kill a motionless player are `via: body`.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: A player who walks inside the champion watches a 1.75 m greatsword sweep over their head and loses 96 hit points to the chest that walked through them, and a spearman standing at 1.22 m cannot be hit by anything at all.

remedy.action: Two changes, in this order. (1) Fix the weapon volume rather than compensating for it. At the champion's first active frame the chop's socket capsule spans z = [1.34, 2.57] with the root at z = 0.384, i.e. the blade's near end is 0.95 m in front of its own root and never re-enters the 0.4-1.1 m band. Give the enemy archetypes' `chop_overhead` and `thrust` clip archetypes in game/data/combat/clips.json a low phase — a follow-through that brings the guard socket down through the attacker's own front quarter — so the swept hull covers the band the attacker is walking through. Verify with `--root-dz 0`, which isolates the blade from the corridor. (2) Stop the body corridor paying the weapon's damage. Give `hitgeometry.json §body_hazard` its own `motion_value` and `poise_damage` (a shoulder-check is a shove, not a cut) and resolve it against `struck_part` with that value in game/src/combat/resolve.js step 8b, so a trace reader and a player can tell the two apart. Then re-run the contiguity acceptance: with the weapon volume fixed, the spear's and halberd's dead ring disappears because the blade band now starts inside the corridor's outer edge.

remedy.acceptance: With `hitgeometry.json §body_hazard` removed, `min_hit_distance_m <= 0.35 m` for all four champion attacks and for all seven player weapon classes, `root_dz_m` unchanged. With it present, every attack's hit band is contiguous from 0.05 m for all eleven attacks (4 enemy + 7 player), no interior gap at any 0.05 m step. A body hit's `dmg` is strictly less than the same attack's weapon `dmg` in the trace. And in the browser turtle, the majority of hits taken carry `via: "weapon"` rather than `via: "body"`.

secondary_observations.what: THE NODE ARENA IS NOT THE GAME AFTER ABOUT 300 FRAMES, AND ITS FIDELITY CLAIM IS UNCHECKED. tools/lib/combat-node.mjs states that `cmb-reach.mjs --verify` runs a sample of rows through both and fails if they differ. That flag does not exist — `grep -n verify tools/harness/cmb-reach.mjs` returns only the comment asserting it, and passing --verify is silently ignored (exit 0). I checked it instead. Reach agrees exactly, browser and node, on all eleven attacks including both interior gaps and the 0.5987 m contact distance. Long fights do not: NodeArena.step() calls CombatSystem.step alone, while sim/step.js stepOnce() also runs stepWorldCollision, settleWorld, encounters, skill use, NPCs, the stealth system, route and camera, plus the one seeded RNG draw. EnemyController._idleBehaviour steers toward the player at 240 dps only while `alertState === 'AGGRO'`, and alertState is written by sim/stealth/system.js::stepPerception(). In the node arena it is never AGGRO, so the champion never turns between attacks; by frame 1700 its yaw has drifted 85.5 degrees off the player. Frame-by-frame the two are identical for 194 frames, then diverge. The consequence is that tools/harness/cmb-reach.mjs --probe turtle — the acceptance instrument this whole remediation is graded on, and the source of reports/w1-09/cmb-reach.json — measures a fight the game does not have.

THE TURTLE DOES NOT WIN, AND THE BUILD'S OWN CAVEAT IS WRONG IN THE OTHER DIRECTION. reports/w1-09/cmb-reach.json says a motionless mashing player kills the 2,876-HP champion at every stand distance from 0.4 m to 2.6 m taking 46-90% of its health. Replaying that exact configuration through window.__HARNESS in headless Chromium, at three input phases across seven stand distances: the player DIES in all 21 runs, in 27.6-33.7 s, with the champion on 1628-2069 of 2876. With a harder cadence of my own across nine distances including the 0.0 m and 0.2 m that cmb-reach never tests, all nine die too, in 33.4-41.0 s. The acceptance the round-2 gap set — 'a motionless mashing player at 0.8-1.5 m taking >= 0.4 x max HP' — is met in the shipping game by a wide margin. It is met by the body corridor: 5 to 7 of the 8 hits that kill it are `via: body`.

THE EXEMPLAR'S DANGER SURVIVES WITHOUT A KNOB — VERIFIED TWICE, AND THIS IS THE ROUND'S BEST RESULT. `eatRate` really is gone. `--greed-scale 0`, which the build offers as its own falsification, leaves row 13 at 0.125 and row 14 at 0.687, both in band. I then went looking for the successor knob and found the candidate: `wobble`, the 2-5 frame random jitter on the bot's roll lead. I copied cmb-exemplar.mjs, added a --wobble flag that changes nothing else, and ran it at 0 — a bot that rolls at a fixed lead every single time. Rows 13 and 14 come out at 0.143 and 0.842, and 0.842 is the shipped median to the digit. Neither greed nor the jitter drives the damage. Round 1's exemplar had no danger, round 2's was a constant, round 3's is a consequence.

THE EXEMPLAR REGRESSED WHERE NOBODY WAS LOOKING. Round 2's independently written recompute tool, run on round 3's traces, puts the exemplar at 18 of 24 banded rows against the 21 of 24 it measured on round 2's build. Four rows that were in band are out: row 16 (frames at exactly 0 stamina) 130 -> 0, row 17 (% frames below 25% stamina) 0.1406 -> 0.0127, row 22 (committed-frame ratio) 0.4144 -> 0.6462, and row 28 (inputs dropped for insufficient stamina) 32 -> 0, which is the item's own automatic fail. The stamina economy did not degrade; it stopped. The build's status file lists rows 16/17/22/28 as 'STILL OPEN', which reads as pre-existing. They are not.

THE ROUND-2 CRITIC'S OWN REACH PROBE NOW SILENTLY READS ZERO, AND IT IS NOT AN ENGINE FINDING. tools/harness/critic-w1-09-r2.mjs --probe reach reports that chop, thrust and combo_a hit at NO distance from 0.0 to 4.0 m on this build. The cause is that Engine.setEntityPos() accepts and ignores opts.yaw, which was harmless in round 2 because the enemy snapped its facing to the player's bearing on the frame an attack began; round 3 correctly removed that snap, so the probe now aims the champion away from its target. Recorded here so that no later critic re-runs that instrument and reports a catastrophe. Re-spawn with spawn(id, x, z, {yaw}) instead — Engine.spawn does honour it. Separately: Engine.setEntityPos()'s ignored yaw is a live harness defect and should either honour the argument or throw.

corpus_extended.note: RI-MTH07 makes a critic prove that a MODEL is consumed by the world. It says nothing about an INSTRUMENT that claims to reproduce the world. This build shipped tools/lib/combat-node.mjs, a headless arena 500x faster than the browser, adopted it for the acceptance measurement, and asserted in two files that a --verify flag checks it against window.__HARNESS. The flag does not exist, and the arena diverges from the game after 194 frames because it runs CombatSystem.step alone while the engine's fixed step also runs stealth perception, which is what makes the enemy turn. Proposed addition: any harness that reimplements or partially instantiates the simulation must ship a VERIFY mode that replays N sampled scenarios through the shipping entry point and fails on any divergence, and a critic may not cite a number from such a harness without running it.

M2's substep rationale ('Reducing them to 1 changes which attacks connect') is stated in the data file and is measurably false on this build: 4 -> 1 leaves the hit set byte-identical across 71 distances. Proposed M2c: the substep count must be validated by ablation — a build must show at least one (attack, distance) pair whose outcome changes between substeps 1 and the shipped value, or the substep count is unjustified and the sweep is not continuous.

Three defects, two carried from round 2. (a) '24 rows that carry a band' versus §D's 25-26 lets an implementation pick its own denominator; enumerate them by number. (b) M2 says 'median over >= 5 fights' without saying median of WHAT — this build takes the median of each row and counts the result (18 of 25), where the median of the per-fight counts is 17. State which. (c) M3(d)'s pack is coarse enough that a build can win it while failing the underlying statistic; add the 90th-percentile invulnerable-frame-to-nearest-hitbox-frame distance as a second, numeric discriminator with a stated band.

Re-filed from round 2 and still open. The AP table fails damage with no hitbox; nothing fails a scenario `face` directive that the tracking steer overrides from frame 2, so an authored heading is not honoured and no check notices. Proposed AP13: an authored heading must hold for the whole animation.

arbitration_questions.question: S26 as amended authorises a body corridor that resolves 'through the identical order (i-frames, block cone, dedup, poise, damage)'. It does not say the corridor should deal the WEAPON's damage. Measured, it does: the champion's chop deals 96 whether the blade cuts you at 3.65 m or its chest walks through you at 0.05 m, and the same holds for every player weapon. Is a shoulder-check that deals a greatsword's damage inside S26's intent, or does the ruling need a clause giving the body hazard its own motion value? I have not invented a ruling; I have scored the measured consequence under RI-CMB04 and named it as the biggest gap.
sides: S26 says 'use the same VOLUME for pushing and for hitting' and gives a reason — the dead ring. It says nothing about the damage number, so the builder's reading is defensible.

A body hazard that pays the weapon's damage makes the weapon's geometry irrelevant at close range, which is exactly the state S26 was written to end. It also makes the `via` field in the trace a distinction without a difference for the player.

The one that ran landed on OURS, so §2.5 fired: recorded, re-examined at frame resolution with a second discriminator, and the outcome recorded in blind_comparisons[0].rerun. The escalation ladder was used in full and it is what found the divergence: zoom (frame-by-frame instead of per-fight), change the sample (0.0 and 0.2 m, which the build's own turtle probe never tests), stress it (attacks back-to-back at each move's own total instead of every 160 frames, and three input phases), second-order (not 'does the body hazard hit' but 'what is it that hits, and for how much'), and first-minute-versus-tenth-hour (the spear's dead ring at 1.22 m is a tenth-hour discovery; the shoulder-check for 96 is a first-minute one). I read the builder's status file before measuring, which is a departure from CRITIC-DOCTRINE §8 and is recorded honestly in critic.saw_builder_notes_before_blind; it was supplied in the dispatch as a list of claims to disprove, and every one of them was re-measured with an instrument written by me rather than accepted.
